problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x-3)(y+1)^{2}.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=x(2-y).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)>0?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=2.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have a strict inequality, we use dashed lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/41f10e527834d0767709b965150054a564eaee9c174204381ed94b0e43077fe0.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/994e35e23e56191ef06a155912a326d28d857f236308655265d18d17bb48531b.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $x$ | $(2-y)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,3)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,3)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)>0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/9710358526e0e14fbf7263ba5d1496cdcb2941f9cb32a1d07b2ea37865163ab2.png)
